chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Khalid ibn Ayman al-Hannat, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The man is not made to swear an oath except upon what is based upon his knowledge.

key_terms.يُسْتَحْلَفُ: is made to swear / is compelled to take an oath

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for making a man swear an oath according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from al-Kafi delineates the scope of *istihlaf* (compelling an oath), restricting it to facts within the individual's direct knowledge (*ilm*) rather than hearsay or speculation. This principle safeguards against perjury and ensures judicial accuracy, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on precision in legal testimony and oath-taking procedures.
